summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. DR-011 is the row where a parent-level selection could most easily be read as reaching sixteen residuals, and this entry refuses that on every surface — including one refusal I have not seen elsewhere, that a coordinator-composed residual CLOSED is unlawful, extending DR-204 from SATISFIED to closure. Its status claim is precise rather than convenient: I checked all sixteen residual rows and found fourteen OPEN, two NARROWED and none CLOSED, which is exactly what 'OPEN, NARROWED, or otherwise not CLOSED' asserts. The check-c2-v12 rejection is well-founded at source — the freeze records that validator as UNREVIEWED and R03 is OPEN. All three measured inputs verify against a file 08 that has moved because D-081's edit landed, and I confirmed that edit against the register rather than assuming it.
whatIVerified: Prompt digest at start and end: 40ae63c6bf554f3952221511fd07c71fce8194f4470f3da6c66ef5ae21b3e56a, equal to the dispatch-supplied value. Subject at a07fcbb6c23c8adfdf5cb43bcef60e4ffc918aa0725e95b2a549b1c679aaf171, equal to both the dispatch and the prompt. Three measurements each at start and again at end; both -r--r--r-- at both ends.

The attack 'closes any residual R01–R16' fails, and I tested the underlying status claim rather than the refusal language. Reading every DR-011 residual row in live file 08: R01, R02, R03, R04, R05, R08, R09, R10, R11, R12, R13, R14, R15 and R16 are OPEN; R06 and R07 are NARROWED — 'application half closed, validator-standing and join remaining' — and none is CLOSED. The entry's formulation 'Residuals R01–R16 remain individually OPEN, NARROWED, or otherwise not CLOSED' is therefore exact, and the word NARROWED is doing real work rather than hedging: it is the actual status of two rows.

The refusal is stated four ways: the header 'Does not close any DR-011 residual'; clause 2 'It does not close, dispose, or reclassify any residual DR-011-R01 through DR-011-R16'; clause 3 'Every residual remains owed on the authoritative path. A green checker still cannot elevate a residual'; and clause 6 'Closes no residual … may discharge condition 1 for DR-011 within the scope it names, while residuals stay OPEN.'

Clause 5 carries a refusal I have not seen in the earlier selection entries and which this row specifically needs: 'A coordinator-composed SATISFIED is unlawful (DR-204). A coordinator-composed residual CLOSED is also unlawful.' The second sentence extends DR-204's rule from row-level SATISFIED to residual closure, which is the move a sixteen-residual parent selection would otherwise leave unguarded.

The attack 'treats check-c2-v12 ACCEPT-STANDING as R03 CLOSED' fails, and the rejection is correct at source rather than merely asserted. The alternatives section rejects it because 'standing of an instrument is not residual closure; that review's own advisories remain.' IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE records that 'The named validator is now **check-c2-v12.py**, and it is **UNREVIEWED** — no review artifact in this corpus names it', and the claim matrix draws the same distinction in one line: 'artifact review PASS, 0 blockers; named check-c2-v12.py is unreviewed'. file 08's R03 row is OPEN and describes exactly this — 'a checker-review/subject-standing mismatch surfaced in the claim matrix and status manifest'.

The four residual-specific consequences in clause 4 all check out against source. R01: COORD routes it as the 'FACT-PLANE successor closing subject-set agreement, the sufficiency view type…', consistent with 'Facts/Coverage design stays blocked where R01 says so'. R10: COORD reads 'R10 the final blind consumer-B litmus — structurally LAST', matching 'R10 remains structurally last on that path'. R12: COORD reads 'R12 evaluation-proof BOTH halves (MF-4)' and file 08's R12 row describes 'non-interchangeable heads', matching 'Evaluation-proof dual-head (R12) stays unrepaired'. R16: COORD reads 'DR-010 route C PREFERENCE-LADEN (P-1/P-2/G3 successor, jointly with DR-117 and R16)', matching 'Product boundary (R16) stays on Route C'.

The premise about the register's current state is true, and I verified it against the edited file 08 rather than the version I last reviewed. D-081's edit has landed: the regeneration preamble now reads 'one SATISFIED and nine explicitly disposed' with the stale 'six' gone, the condition-1 row reads '1 of 11 SATISFIED; 9 of 11 explicitly disposed' naming DR-002 through DR-010, and 'DR-011 remains without SATISFIED or scoped owner-recorded disposition'. DR-006, DR-007 and DR-009 now each carry one preview-scope note and DR-011 carries none. So the entry's 'D-081's condition-1 row names DR-011 as the sole unresolved of the eleven' is accurate.

The attack 'counts DR-011 as already disposed' fails: the entry is a selection, states 'Writes no disposition', and its readiness effect is 'Zero at adoption'. Its own preamble names DR-011 as the row with 'no Route B selection and no SATISFIED', which is consistent with the register.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED of DR-011' fails: the header refuses SATISFIED, clause 6 states 'Marks nothing SATISFIED', and the alternatives reject closing residuals by selection on the ground that 'file 08 forbids SATISFIED of DR-011 while any residual is OPEN' — which matches file 08's DR-011 acceptance cell, requiring every residual to be CLOSED by its owning V1 authority or LAWFULLY-DISPOSED with scope, rationale, evidence, reviewer and blueprint effect.

All three measured inputs match live bytes: COORD edec3c70…, file 08 at its new post-D-081 value 1360a4f8…, and the D-081 commit b1885620232c1f3c01a213916fcd6a390d24c0ea, which resolves to 'D-081: file-08 notes for DR-006/007/009 owner recordings'. The file 08 pin was re-measured rather than carried from the pre-edit value.
The owner role is an exact string match: file 08's DR-011 owner cell reads 'V1 coordinator and each surface owner' and the entry pins the identical string.

The exclusion list is complete and correctly bounded: clause 2 excludes DR-002 through DR-010, nine rows, omitting DR-001 because it is SATISFIED and DR-011 because it is this entry's own subject. That matches the pattern I verified in the D-069/D-071/D-072 cycle.

The cycle framing is accurate: D-028, D-047 and D-048 are present and ADOPTED as the cited form precedents; D-051/D-052/D-053 is headed '(CONTESTED)' as the entry states; and D-069, D-071 and D-072 are present and ADOPTED as the separate successor cycle. D-055 is not yet in COORD, so there is no numbering collision.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: clause 6 preserves 'Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization' and 'Authorizes no blueprint'; file 08 measures at its cited digest and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture. I wrote one file and edited and committed nothing.

Reversibility matches the selection form used by the adopted precedents: 'Total before any dependent disposition lands. After one lands, overturn also requires that disposition's owning-authority supersession. Overturn: C-D055.'

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. DR-011 is the hardest row to select on, because a parent-level selection sits directly above sixteen residuals and the tempting error is to let the parent's route imply something about them. This entry refuses that four separate ways and adds a fifth guard I have not seen in the earlier selections — that a coordinator-composed residual CLOSED is unlawful, not just a coordinator-composed SATISFIED. Its status claim is the kind I would normally expect to find loose, and it is not: fourteen OPEN, two NARROWED, none CLOSED, exactly as worded. Two premises I checked against sources rather than accepting — that check-c2-v12's standing is not R03 closure, which the freeze supports by recording that validator UNREVIEWED, and that D-081's edit has landed leaving DR-011 the sole unresolved row, which the edited register confirms.
